concept: Local Inference Micro-Architectures: Signaling, Quantization Superblocks, and Kernel Pipeline Scheduling
summary: Source-anchored research for Local Inference Micro-Architectures: Signaling, Quantization Superblocks, and Kernel Pipeline Scheduling. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Key vectors in transformer self-attention contain sensitive channel-specific magnitude spikes that cause severe perplexity degradation if quantized uniformly with standard symmetric rounding. (high confidence)
PCIe protocol tunneling encapsulates Transaction Layer Packets (TLPs) into transport frames, incurring packet assembly and disassembly overhead at host and device controllers. (high confidence)

Super-block K-quants (Q4_K) group 256 weights into chunks with a shared FP16 super-block scale and eight 6-bit sub-block scales, reducing quantization noise in attention projection layers. (high confidence)

Asymmetric KV cache quantization preserves key vector outlier dimensions in FP8 or FP16 while quantizing value vectors to 4-bit affine blocks, reducing KV memory by up to 70% with less than 0.1 perplexity delta. (high confidence)

Synchronously blocking CPU execution on MTLCommandBuffer waitUntilCompleted() prevents overlapping CPU dispatch with GPU execution, causing up to 25% throughput degradation on small models. (high confidence)
When speculative verification achieves an acceptance rate greater than 60%, end-to-end token generation throughput increases by 25% to 45% on memory-bandwidth-constrained devices. (high confidence)
PAM3 signaling achieves a 50% data rate improvement over binary NRZ at identical Nyquist frequencies by encoding three voltage levels into two transmitted unit intervals. (high confidence)

Speculative decoding amortizes parameter weight memory loading across K candidate tokens by evaluating candidate sequences as a small parallel GEMM batch instead of K sequential GEMV reads. (high confidence)

Retimer jitter and transport layer flow control credits cause non-deterministic round-trip DMA completion times, necessitating large contiguous transfers rather than layer-by-layer handshakes. (high confidence)
Prompt pre-fill evaluates GEMM operations where high arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte > 100) saturates GPU tensor cores and scales linearly with compute clock frequencies. (high confidence)

Auto-regressive decoding executes GEMV operations with minimal arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte approx. 1), causing GPU compute ALUs to sit idle while awaiting memory bus DRAM/GDDR reads. (high confidence)

Runtime compilation of Metal compute shaders creates hitches during initial token generation; caching compiled pipeline states in an MTLBinaryArchive eliminates shader compilation latency. (high confidence)

GDDR7 splits each physical device channel into dual independent 16-bit sub-channels, enabling concurrent burst accesses that avoid bank collision stalls during attention matrix reads. (high confidence)
MTLResourceStorageModeShared allocates memory in a unified system pool coherent between CPU and Metal GPU execution units without explicit cache flush instructions on Apple Silicon. (high confidence)

Passing unified buffer pointers between host Python runtimes and Metal compute kernels enables zero-copy tensor evaluation, reducing kernel invocation latency to sub-microsecond levels. (high confidence)
32-byte memory alignment prevents unaligned memory access penalties and cacheline splits during vectorized 256-bit SIMD load instructions across host CPU and GPU threads. (high confidence)
